newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks seen remaining weak on rupiah.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks seen remaining weak on rupiah.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are seen remaining weak on Thursday due to worries over the central bank's tight rupiah policy, which has prompted banks to raise interest rates, brokers said.
"Concerns remain on the central bank's tight rupiah policy which prompted banks to raise interest rates," one broker said.
Brokers said the worries had sent the Jakarta composite index plunging on Wednesday, closing down 14.02 points, or 1.96 percent, at 699.86 points.
They, however, said bargain-hunting was likely in some fundamentally sound blue chips, but trading volume was likely to be thin.
Brokers said Kyoei Steel was likely to remain among the most active stocks following a modest debut amid generally weak market sentiment on Wednesday.
Property stocks in particular were likely to remain under strong selling pressure due to the concerns over the higher interest rates, brokers said.
The central bank's move, however, tightened rupiah liquidity, pushed up the rupiah interbank rate and prompted banks to increase interest rates, analysts said.

Keeling said some 6.74 trillion rupiah in rights issue payments over the next four weeks and new margin finance regulations limiting domestic retail client coverage were among the main reasons for the falls.
Most blue chips including BII, Indosat and Gudang Garam fell sharply due to worries, brokers said. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
